claims.original_excerpt: die fast 30 Jahre alten Grundlagen der Fahrausbildung
claims.claim_en: The core foundations of German driving training date back almost 30 years.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Last comprehensive reform of goals, content and didactic principles in 1998; later amendments acknowledged.

claims.explanation: 1998 to September 2026 is about 28 years. The wording concerns foundations, not an assertion that no rules have changed since.
claims.limits: A targeted primary-source review was performed, not an exhaustive systematic review. Missing or indirect evidence is not proof of error.

claims.claim_en: For 76% of the representative ACE/forsa sample, good training quality comes first.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: 76% call quality and road preparation very important; 60% call cost very important. Sample 1,001 German-speaking adults, 10–16 December 2025, forsa.omninet.

claims.explanation: Quality is the highest rated consideration in the reported importance ratings. The ordinary priority reading is supported.
claims.limits: This was not a forced first-choice ranking: respondents rated each item independently. It does not show that 76% exclusively rank quality above cost; survey concerns adults, not only pupils.

claims.claim_en: The proposed lay-practice trial is five years and has no mandatory halfway report.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.locator: FahrPraxAnlV § 11, physical p. 31; Article 9, physical p. 53
evidence.summary: Trial authorisations expire at end of fifth year; whole ordinance evaluation within five years.
BASt evaluation and report by end of fourth year.

claims.explanation: No mandatory 2.5-year interim report appears in the recovered texts. The claim must not be read as denying the fourth-year statutory report.
claims.limits: The June 2026 ordinance and July 2026 bill predate the response, but the precise ordinance bytes considered by the author and actual delivery are not authenticated.

claims.claim_en: At least six professional practical units are required before lay practice starts.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Passed theory, six practical units and joint theoretical induction required.

claims.explanation: Matches the recovered operative text.
claims.limits: The June 2026 ordinance and July 2026 bill predate the response, but the precise ordinance bytes considered by the author and actual delivery are not authenticated.

claims.claim_en: Six lessons alone do not ensure sufficient driving competence before lay practice.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Six-unit minimum is described as basic preparation; joint induction and later professional lessons also required.
Individual learning progress requires assessment; no universal six-lesson competence threshold measured.

claims.explanation: The concern is reasonable, but the sources do not measure a universally adequate threshold or show the actual distribution of competence at six units. Minimum lesson count and individual competence are distinct.
claims.limits: Do not infer that the author denies other safeguards or claims every learner is unsafe.

claims.original_excerpt: Forderung des Bundesrates nach einer Opt-Out-Möglichkeit
claims.claim_en: The Bundesrat requests opt-out rather than the bill’s state opt-in system.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.locator: Annex 3 point 4, physical p. 90; government response physical p. 100
evidence.summary: Bundesrat explicitly proposes opt-out, government rejects it.

claims.explanation: Directly matches the two institutional positions.
claims.limits: The June 2026 ordinance and July 2026 bill predate the response, but the precise ordinance bytes considered by the author and actual delivery are not authenticated.

claims.claim_en: Hazard perception, reflection and exchange need pedagogically guided interactive learning in addition to factual exam preparation.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Recommends blended learning and differentiated teaching; German modality effectiveness evidence sparse.
Randomised curriculum-matched instruction comparison finds no significant attitude difference in properly assigned subgroup; no adequate road-test or crash outcome.

claims.explanation: Research supports the value of instructional design and feedback, but does not establish that all these outcomes require a prescribed interactive modality. Retain the necessity claim without converting recommendations into causal proof.
claims.limits: DFA and ACE discuss self-study quality, not a categorical ban on all online interactive teaching.

claims.claim_en: Only 47% of 18–29-year-olds support abolition of mandatory classroom presence, below a majority in the survey.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: 47% in age 18–29 regard abolition and fully digital learning as very/rather sensible.

claims.explanation: Matches the reported subgroup point estimate.
claims.limits: Age-cell sample size and confidence interval are not given; this is a survey estimate, not proof that population support is below 50%.

claims.claim_en: Each avoided repeat examination saves about €600.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Separates training, professional fees, application and private practice costs; no national €600-per-retake estimate.
National average total €3,400 and multiple cost components, not retake-cost distribution.

claims.explanation: A repeat practical examination can entail examination and school presentation fees plus further lessons. The universal approximate saving cannot be authenticated from the recovered primary sources.
claims.limits: Exam class/type, local school prices and number of additional lessons are unspecified. A single statutory exam fee would not capture total retake expense.

claims.claim_en: The ordinance proposes a mandatory documented practical test-readiness assessment.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: At least one exam-like public-road journey, full exam duration, documented assessment before accompanying candidate to exam.

claims.explanation: Matches operative safeguards.
claims.limits: The June 2026 ordinance and July 2026 bill predate the response, but the precise ordinance bytes considered by the author and actual delivery are not authenticated.

claims.claim_en: Structured learning-progress checks during ordinary practical instruction are missing, while lay practice has an observation drive.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.locator: FahrschAusbV § 4 and Annex 1, physical pp. 10–12, 18; FahrPraxAnlV § 7, p. 29
evidence.summary: General learner-oriented instruction criteria and final assessment; explicit observation drive after 500–600 km for lay practice.
Current law already requires discussion of level and documentation.
Systematic progress diagnostics still proposed as an improvement.

claims.explanation: Supported as the contextual comparison of a defined structured interim checkpoint with ordinary instruction. Existing duties to discuss/document progress must be preserved.
claims.limits: Not a claim that instructors perform no assessment, or that current law contains no documentation duties. Draft identity qualified.

claims.claim_en: The reform provides for publishing school prices and practical pass rates.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Prices reported to ministry; public comparison including practical pass rates contemplated.

claims.explanation: The proposed framework supports the description; implementation details remain delegated.
claims.limits: The June 2026 ordinance and July 2026 bill predate the response, but the precise ordinance bytes considered by the author and actual delivery are not authenticated.

claims.claim_en: There are around 10,000 schools with 17,000 branches in Germany.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Estimates 9,665 enterprises and 17,750 total sites: 10,325 main sites plus 7,425 secondary sites.

claims.explanation: The approximate enterprise count is corroborated. The branch count depends on whether Filialen means all locations or strictly secondary branches. The primary comparator counts total sites, not 17,000 secondary sites.
claims.limits: Ordinary colloquial site usage is plausible; denominator ambiguity prevents a conservative error finding.

claims.original_excerpt: wer die Angaben auf Aktualität und Richtigkeit
claims.claim_en: How complete, current and accurate price/pass-rate reporting will be assured is still unclear.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Framework reporting and supervision powers exist; detailed operation delegated.

claims.explanation: The recovered bill does not resolve all implementation questions, but an absence claim across every implementation instrument cannot be established.
claims.limits: Treat practical uncertainty as the author’s implementation concern, not proof that no public authority has responsibility.

claims.claim_en: The proposed reduction removes five minutes of on-road driving from the class B practical examination.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Current class B: total 55 minutes, driving 30 minutes.
Proposed class B: total 40 minutes, driving 25 minutes.

claims.explanation: On-road time falls by five minutes. Total exam duration is a separate 15-minute change.
claims.limits: Current consolidated FeV header last amended 12 August 2026; precise September ordinance version remains qualified.

claims.claim_en: Reducing driving time reduces opportunities to observe relevant situations and assess competence reliably.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Defines present observation time.
Cuts road-driving minimum; no direct reliability estimate established in passages checked.

claims.explanation: Fewer observation minutes are mechanically true, but whether reliability materially declines depends on test design and observations per minute. No direct comparative validation recovered.
claims.limits: Risk magnitude and claimed small financial advantage are evaluative; do not treat risk warning as a demonstrated crash outcome.

claims.claim_en: Many training and testing requirements change together, complicating isolation of individual measures’ effects.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Parallel changes to theory, simulator use, special drives, lay practice and examination duration, with evaluation.

claims.explanation: Simultaneous interventions can confound attribution in an uncontrolled before/after evaluation. This supports the conditional identification concern.
claims.limits: A properly designed comparison could still identify effects; the statement does not prove evaluation will fail.

claims.claim_en: Lay practice requires a passed theory test and therefore, for BF17, cannot begin earlier than three months before age 17 under current timing rules.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Requires passed theory test.
Theory max three months before minimum age; BF17 minimum 17.

claims.explanation: Matches combined requirements for the BF17 route.
claims.limits: Not all lay-practice candidates seek BF17. Joint induction and initial lessons must also occur.

claims.claim_en: Before completion, the BF17 lay route requires at least 1,000 km, observation, further professional instruction and the practical exam.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Observation after 500–600 km; at least six more units; total at least 1,000 km and any further instruction needed.
Practical test after training and theory.

claims.explanation: The stated components match. Completing them before age 17 is necessary only to obtain the maximum BF17 period, not a legal three-month expiry.
claims.limits: Read the short period in context of starting BF17 at the 17th birthday; it is not a mandatory deadline for every learner.

claims.claim_en: Longer accompanied experience is a central safety advantage of BF17.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.locator: Primary ministry release, 12 July 2007, evaluation results
evidence.summary: Observational comparison finds 28.5% fewer accidents after solo driving; more than six months accompanied period associated with greater reductions.

claims.explanation: Primary evaluation supports experience-building as a relevant mechanism and lower subsequent accident association.
claims.limits: Nonrandomised evaluation and possible selection/confounding prevent assigning all benefit solely to duration. It does not measure the new pre-test lay regime.

claims.claim_en: The package’s lay-practice cost example compares a minimum-lesson reform scenario with typical existing training costs.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Baseline 35 units from median in M330; reform recipe six initial and six further units plus assessment/induction. Explicit example because uptake unknown.

claims.explanation: The methodological description is broadly right: specified low-lesson example versus a typical baseline. The baseline is a median, and the source labels the reform case illustrative rather than a population forecast.
claims.limits: Do not infer the bill claims every pupil saves that amount. ACE uses Gesetzentwurf loosely for the related package; detailed example is in June ordinance.

claims.claim_en: More required professional practical lessons increase a learner’s total cost, other components held fixed.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Per-unit fees multiplied by number of ordinary and special lessons.

claims.explanation: Follows from the explicit fee model.
claims.limits: This is a conditional cost mechanism, not a prediction of actual uptake, lesson counts or net national saving.

claims.original_excerpt: ein geeignetes Fahrzeug und eine Begleitperson
claims.claim_en: Access to a suitable vehicle and eligible companion is required to benefit from lay practice.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Vehicle/insurance conditions and named eligible companion required.

claims.explanation: The legal and practical access prerequisite is supported.
claims.limits: The further prediction that low-income pupils will benefit less is excluded as a forecast; these provisions alone do not estimate inequality.

claims.claim_en: The 2018 instructor reform organised training into competence areas and expanded training.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: 2018 framework, introduction, seven-month 1,100-unit course, placement and reflection, competence-based curriculum.

evidence.locator: Historical discussion of instructor reform and assessment, printed pp. 13–17, 60–61
evidence.summary: 2018 pedagogical reforms and strengthening evaluation competences described.

claims.explanation: Official curriculum and research history corroborate the qualitative reform description.
claims.limits: No precise increment or comparison year is claimed. This does not prove all current instructors completed the new course.

claims.claim_en: Pedagogical and psychological content takes almost half the total instructor-training hours.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: 525 pedagogical/psychological units out of 1,080 curriculum units, about 48.6%. § 1 additionally includes introduction, placement and reflection.

claims.explanation: Supported in the ordinary curricular-hours context of the preceding sentence about training content.
claims.limits: Including introductory, placement and reflection hours would yield a lower proportion; the denominator is the theoretical curriculum, not every hour of the entire qualification pathway.

claims.claim_en: The BMV previously posted the exact quoted statement prioritising increased road safety.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Ministry says training quality must remain and road safety must not be harmed.

claims.explanation: The ministry’s published safety commitment is corroborated, but the exact historical webpage sentence and removal date were not recovered.
claims.limits: A source-access or historical-page gap is not evidence that the author fabricated the quotation.

claims.claim_en: The ministry published its cost-reduction reform proposals on 16 October 2025 at a press conference.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.locator: Dated cover and contents, physical pp. 1–3
evidence.summary: Official dated reform points publish the listed proposals.

claims.explanation: The official document is dated 16 October 2025 and contains the proposals.
claims.limits: The exact press-conference event is not independently reconstructed; no material contrary evidence, and publication timing is directly corroborated.

claims.claim_en: Theoretical driver education teaches rules and also forms attitudes and values relevant to safe participation.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Curriculum includes partners, emotions, risk, responsibility, self-assessment and interaction.
Affective goals and reflection are part of the training concept.

claims.explanation: The stated functions and learning objectives are supported.
claims.limits: This does not establish that every real course successfully changes attitudes or that only presence can do so.

claims.claim_en: Accidents and traffic misconduct arise more from adverse rule-compliance attitudes than deficient rule knowledge.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.locator: Training goals and learner characteristics; section 4.2
evidence.summary: Attitudes and knowledge both recognised; no directly comparable causal population attribution for these two categories.
Attitude/knowledge tests do not establish relative causes of crashes.

claims.explanation: The comparative causal claim needs a defined population and method for apportioning causes. The recovered evidence does not establish that ranking.
claims.limits: No claim of falsity or intent follows from lack of an appropriate causal denominator.

claims.original_excerpt: Die Pflicht zum Präsenzunterricht soll zukünftig entfallen
claims.claim_en: The reform allows fully digital theory preparation instead of compulsory physical presence.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Presence, synchronous, asynchronous e-learning or combinations available to learner; schools need not offer every format.
Explicitly proposes abolishing mandatory presence and fully digital learning.

claims.explanation: Matches proposed options, not a mandate for everyone to learn alone.
claims.limits: The June 2026 ordinance and July 2026 bill predate the response, but the precise ordinance bytes considered by the author and actual delivery are not authenticated.

claims.claim_en: Memorising the question bank can enable passing the theory test, but such preparation cannot develop practical preparation or attitudes.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Distinguishes factual learning and deeper application; no experiment isolating pure memorisation against practical/attitude outcomes.
Matched curricula and random assignment, not a pure memorisation intervention; no adequate practical-test outcome.

claims.explanation: Rote success and limited transfer are plausible, but the zero-transfer/zero-attitude proposition is not established by these designs.
claims.limits: The word so refers to pure memorisation, not all online instruction. Do not use successful digital instruction as a direct refutation.

claims.claim_en: Limited digital competence, access or learning ability can hinder self-directed digital preparation.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Learner background, motivation and self-regulation matter; some learners need guidance; adaptation may also assist low-literacy learners.

claims.explanation: The conditional mechanism is supported. The sentence’s predicted actual exclusion is separately excluded as a forecast.
claims.limits: Not proof that all disadvantaged pupils are excluded or that digital learning is always worse; available support and design can mitigate barriers.

claims.original_excerpt: eine positive Lernatmosphäre hat nachweislich Auswirkungen
claims.claim_en: A positive learning atmosphere improves cognition, knowledge uptake, motivation and interaction.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Teaching quality and learner engagement are relevant; source combines literature, theory and proposed curriculum.

claims.explanation: A broad pedagogical proposition is reasonable, but the checked primary material does not isolate classroom atmosphere as a causal treatment for each listed outcome.
claims.limits: Does not establish that a statutory room specification is necessary; that legal requirement is the author’s preference.

claims.original_excerpt: welche in Präsenz unterrichtet werden müssen
claims.claim_en: BASt OFSA I/II investigations establish which subjects must be taught in person and which can be online.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Sparse driver-specific comparative evidence; recommended blended curriculum allocates content by pedagogical rationale.

claims.explanation: The source supports a reasoned curricular allocation. It does not provide experimental proof that specified subjects cannot be learned in other modalities. The author may mean the recommended model’s allocation.
claims.limits: Because an ordinary recommendation-based reading is plausible, do not classify an empirical overstatement as a finding.

claims.original_excerpt: Präsenzunterricht in Verbindung mit asynchronem E-Learning
claims.claim_en: Combining in-person teaching with asynchronous e-learning can give good learning results and extend/strengthen learning.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: General education comparisons and design principles support blended learning, with heterogeneity and possible extra-time confounding.
Different methods can achieve comparable knowledge and attitude scores; no single universally best method.

claims.explanation: Supported as a capability claim, with instructional quality and learner conditions.
claims.limits: Evidence is not a direct German reform trial or proof that this combination dominates every alternative. The nearly cost-neutral extension is not separately validated.

claims.claim_en: Adding online elements can extend learning time nearly without extra cost.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Self-directed phases extend engagement, but no complete implementation cost evaluation for this proposition.

claims.explanation: Feasible for some existing platforms, but near cost neutrality depends on development, licensing, instructor support and baseline. No primary cost comparison recovered.
claims.limits: Conditional possibility; not evidence of a false national cost figure.

claims.claim_en: Self-directed theory learning requires motivation and structured engagement, particularly for young learners.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Self-regulation, motivation, autonomy and guidance are explicit requirements; not every learner has all prerequisites.

claims.explanation: Supports the mechanism behind the concern.
claims.limits: Age-wide inability and a prediction of lower pass rates are not established and are excluded forecasts.

claims.claim_en: Simulators can reduce early-stage anxiety/stress, practise basic skills and repeat complex scenarios without real-road risk.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Qualitative literature review and competence mapping; protected environment, early preparation, lower/different stress and repeated rare scenarios.

claims.explanation: Supported as potential and functional use, not a quantified effect for all simulator products.
claims.limits: Study reports few robust comparative studies; co-author MOVING archive and technical/didactic assessment do not establish a crash reduction or guaranteed training-time saving.

claims.claim_en: Simulators cannot fully replace complex real-road training.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Transfer and realism limitations; no complete substitution of theory or practical driving.

claims.explanation: Matches the source’s scope and contemporary technical limitations.
claims.limits: Not a claim about all future technology or a prohibition of selected simulator learning.

claims.claim_en: Demand for full manual-car training means schools still need manual vehicles.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Ministry proposes simulator manual competence with automatic-car exam.
Permits a manual training/test pathway.

claims.explanation: A preference for full manual training is plausible, but its prevalence and consequent fleet requirement for every school are not established.
claims.limits: A customer-demand forecast or commercial choice is not an error solely because no survey was recovered.

claims.claim_en: Existing rules on extensions can require a manual-vehicle practical test to avoid an automatic restriction.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: B197 manual-competence route does not give the same prior manual-test exemption for later BE/C/D extensions.

claims.explanation: The extension-rule issue is real under the consolidated law predating the response.
claims.limits: A school offering only basic B need not itself offer every extension; future harmonisation could change rules. Need for every school to retain manual cars is not established.

claims.claim_en: Instructor qualifications require legal, didactic, methodological, communicative and social competence.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Competence areas encompass teaching, assessment, advice, education and technical/legal knowledge.

claims.explanation: Curriculum directly corroborates the qualification requirements.
claims.limits: Requirement does not prove every practising instructor has equal skills, or that lay practice lacks every safeguard.

claims.claim_en: The established German novice-driver system has never included lay training before the professional test, while BF17 is a lawful alternative.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Current BF17 requires the ordinary passed theory/practical tests before accompanied driving.
Current professional pre-test training framework.

claims.explanation: The current distinction is supported. The historical absolute at no time is not authenticated across the system’s full history.
claims.limits: Do not substitute current law for a universal historical claim or treat BF17 post-test experience as identical to proposed pre-test lay instruction.

claims.claim_en: The ministry’s current reference estimate for class B acquisition is €3,400.
claims.policy_link: Cost, learning quality, safety or feasibility premise in the author’s reform assessment.
claims.check_method: Independent comparison with primary law, draft provisions, original survey tables and/or research methods and results; temporal and contextual reading.

evidence.summary: Official 16 October 2025 paper gives average around €3,400 with regional variation.

claims.explanation: The attributed reference estimate is authentic.
claims.limits: This supports the estimate used in the debate, not a measured price for every learner in September 2026 or a guarantee that future lay practice costs more.

sources.title: ACE commissioned forsa survey release, 27 January 2026
sources.temporal_limit: Retrieved 25 October 2026. Authored responses dated 30 September; source date, methods and legal header require validation. Current snapshots do not prove earlier page bytes.

exclusions.reason: Safety/quality priorities, intermediate-report timing, extra competence check and national opt-out are policy preferences. Their underlying legal and competence premises are inventoried.
Minimum interactive standards, portal/KBA design and documented diagnostics are recommendations; benefits of transparency are conditional expectations without a quantified realised effect.

Predicted delay, lower BF17 uptake, realised savings and distribution by income are forecasts. Earlier test/application timing is a requested change, not a claim current applications cannot be filed six months before minimum age.
Income-tested Führerschein-BAföG design and asserted fairer access are a policy proposal and prospective effects; repeated modernisation/safety priorities add no independent factual claim.
Cover/contact/banking matter incidental. Deklassierung and safety priority are evaluations; inevitable deterioration is a forecast.
Room regulation and social interaction requirements are preferences. Unavoidable future extra lessons/cost and actual exclusion are forecasts; conditional learning/access mechanisms inventoried.

Proposed teaching sequence, mandatory presence and claimed most promising option are curriculum choices; future pass-rate deterioration and universal adolescent incapacity are predictions/evaluations.

Better parental preparation, BF17 expansion and rejection of cost-focus are recommendations. Future accident damage/net cost above €3,400 and road-safety harm are forecasts, not realised facts. Successful/stetig gewachsen wording lacks a defined measurable comparison.
Conclusion and signature repeat normative preferences, with no additional material testable premise.
